description: Metres of fibre wound per metre of beam span
source: Claude estimate scaled from the flax value (550 m/m) by axial stiffness per roving: flax roving ~12 GPa x 1.66 mm2 = 20 kN (Duque Estrada et al. 2026, Sci. Rep. 16:8154: Safilin flax 12 GPa, 1.44 g/cm3); E-glass ~76 GPa x 0.94 mm2 (2.4 g/m / 2.55 g/cm3) = 71 kN, i.e. ~3.6x stiffer per roving. Fibre modulus of E-glass from general knowledge, not re-checked.
comments: Glass needs fewer metres of roving for the same beam stiffness: pure stiffness scaling gives 550/3.6 = ~150 m/m (min). Typical 275 (half the flax value) because CFW layups also need minimum numbers of passes and edge/anchor fibres that do not scale with stiffness; max 550 = same layup as flax. Highly uncertain: Di Bari stress that comparisons should be on equal structural capacity from a structural model; replace with a structural design when available.

description: Mass of one metre of fibre (incl. resin)
source: Gil Pérez et al. 2021, Materials 14:5509 (Univ. Stuttgart, glass-fibre coreless-wound components; elib.uni-stuttgart.de/bitstream/11682/12343): glass roving Owens Corning PipeStrand S2300, 2400 tex; fibre volume ratio 50.0 +- 1.3% (47.5% per component); epoxy Hexion Epikote MGS LR135 + hardeners (1.15 g/cm3 assumed).
comments: Per m of roving: 2.4 g glass + resin at FVR 50%: glass 2.4/2.55 = 0.94 cm3, so resin 0.94 cm3 x 1.15 = 1.08 g; total 3.5 g/m (glass mass share 69%). Glass and epoxy densities (2.55, 1.15 g/cm3) are general values, not re-checked. Range: FVR 55% (3.1 g/m) to 45% (4.0 g/m). 1 m of span = 275 x 0.0035 = 0.96 kg.

source: Design working life 50 y (EN 1990 category 4). Glass/epoxy does not rot and is more moisture-resistant than natural-fibre composites (general knowledge).

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): composted
source: No EU split for GFRP waste found (CompositesUK 2021 FRP circular-economy report names landfill, energy from waste, cement kiln and mechanical recycling as the routes but gives no shares).
